habitat: Singly in open bushveld, plantations and suburbia. It hawks insects from a high perch.
summary: An uncommon resident. A small, nondescript bird, dark brown above, white below with a dusky breast and a white throat, and a black bill. The outer tail feathers are white with brown tips, and there are white patches on the sides of the rump. In display it gives a high insect-like tseet. The call note is a thin trill lasting about four seconds. The Kemp name is Sharpbilled Honeyguide and the code RB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Lesser Honeyguide is larger, with a thick bill and a pale patch at its base. Brown-backed Honeybird is the small brown bird with a black bill and white outer tail.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^10=1024 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 512–2048.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

upperparts.pattern: White patches on the sides of the rump.

underparts.pattern: White below, with a dusky breast.

tail.shape: White outer feathers with brown tips.

viewNotes.note: Small, dark brown above and white below, with a black bill.
Dark brown upper parts. White rump patches show when it hawks.
High-speed chases in display. Brown-tipped white outer tail feathers.
White underparts with a dusky breast.

calls.description: A high-pitched, insect-like tseet during display chases, and a thin trill tirrrrrrrr lasting about four seconds. No grade A recording was in the set. Grade B from Kirstenbosch. The catalogue types it as song and the filename says the file was edited. It was not cleaned again.

research.note: Status is resident and all twelve months are listed. Population figures were left unchanged.
